title: Ohm's Law and Electric Power
learning_goal: Calculate current, voltage, resistance, and power in series and parallel circuits using Ohm's law and power relationships.

stages.title: 1. Voltage, current, and resistance
stages.content: Voltage is electric potential difference, current is the rate of charge flow, and resistance opposes current. Ohm's law relates them: V = IR.

stages.title: 2. Worked example with Ohm's law
stages.content: A 12 V source is connected across a 4 Ω resistor. Using I = V/R, the current is I = 12/4 = 3 A.

stages.title: 3. Electric power
stages.content: Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is transferred. Use P = IV. Equivalent forms include P = I²R and P = V²/R when Ohm's law applies.

stages.title: 4. Apply relationships in circuits
stages.content: In series circuits, current is the same through each resistor. In parallel circuits, voltage is the same across each branch. Use these rules before applying V = IR to individual components.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A device operates at 24 V and draws 2 A. What electrical power does it use?
stages.alternate_explanation: Power tells how quickly electrical energy is transferred, so multiply the potential difference by the current.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, rearrange and use V = IR, calculate P = IV, select the correct current or voltage rule for series and parallel circuits, and check units for volts, amperes, ohms, and watts.

concept_cards.content: Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is transferred. Use P = IV. Equivalent forms include P = I²R and P = V²/R when Ohm's law applies.

concept_cards.title: Apply relationships in circuits

concept_cards.title: An ohmic resistor has 12 V across 4 Ω. What current flows?
concept_cards.content: Use I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A. Ohm’s law assumes the resistor’s resistance is fixed under the stated conditions.

concept_cards.title: A component carries 2 A at a potential difference of 6 V. What electric power is transferred?
concept_cards.content: P = VI = 6 × 2 = 12 W. Power is energy transfer per unit time, not the total energy.
